edge_case_findings.finding: Hook allows docker build with BOTH api-dev.life-ai.app AND api.life-ai.app present in the same command
edge_case_findings.detail: The grep logic is: block if 'api.life-ai.app' present AND 'api-dev.life-ai.app' NOT present. If both are present, it passes. This is acceptable because having api-dev in the command means the dev URL regex matched, and having two --build-arg for HAPPY_SERVER_URL would be unusual/nonsensical.
edge_case_findings.recommendation: No action needed -- edge case is unlikely in practice

findings.finding: WebFetch tool is NOT checked by pretool-block-production.sh despite being registered for it in settings.json
findings.detail: The hook's case statement only matches 'mcp__playwright__browser_navigate' and 'mcp__playwright__browser_click'. When tool_name='WebFetch', the case falls through to '*)' which exits 0 (allow). This means WebFetch to https://life-ai.app or https://api.life-ai.app is silently allowed.
findings.recommendation: Add 'WebFetch' to the case statement in pretool-block-production.sh and extract 'url' from tool_input for URL checking
findings.test_evidence: echo '{"tool_name":"WebFetch","tool_input":{"url":"https://life-ai.app/auth/default"}}' | bash hook -> exit 0 (should be exit 2)

findings.finding: browser_run_code is NOT checked by the hook despite being registered in project settings.json
findings.detail: mcp__playwright__browser_run_code is registered in the project settings.json but the global hook only handles browser_navigate and browser_click. Code like page.goto('https://life-ai.app') inside browser_run_code would not be caught. However, the hook reads tool_input as JSON and greps for URL patterns -- but the case statement exits before reaching that code for browser_run_code.
Correctly blocked by case match on browser_navigate

gaps.finding: curl/wget GET to production API (localhost:3000) is NOT blocked
gaps.detail: The global pretool-bash-safety.sh blocks curl/wget POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE to session/machine endpoints, but does NOT block GET requests to localhost:3000 (production API). A subagent could do 'curl http://localhost:3000/v1/sessions' and read production session data.
gaps.recommendation: Add a rule to block curl/wget to localhost:3000 and api.life-ai.app entirely from dev environment, or at minimum block non-health endpoints. Health checks via localhost:3000/health are used for isolation verification so those may need to remain allowed.
gaps.risk: medium -- read-only access to production data, no mutation

gaps.finding: docker compose restart is blocked globally but docker compose stop is not explicitly checked
gaps.detail: The global hook blocks 'docker.compose (down|restart)' but 'docker compose stop happy-server' is not matched by this pattern. However, 'docker compose stop' is unusual (most use 'docker stop <container>') and docker stop of non-dev containers IS blocked.

gaps.finding: systemctl enable/disable for production services not blocked
gaps.detail: The global hook blocks 'systemctl (stop|restart)' for non-dev services, but 'systemctl disable happy-daemon' or 'systemctl enable' are not checked. These could prevent production services from auto-starting on reboot.
gaps.recommendation: Add 'enable|disable' to the systemctl check, or at least 'disable'

gaps.finding: docker compose up/build for production services is correctly blocked
gaps.detail: Global hook has whitelist-based checking: only applio-*, happy-web-dev, happy-server-dev, postgres-dev, redis-dev are allowed

section_5_project_bash_safety.assessment: This is a lighter version of the global hook, focused on sensitive file writes, destructive disk ops, recursive deletes, and force push warnings. The heavy lifting (docker, systemctl, npm, kill, SQL) is handled by the global hook.
section_5_project_bash_safety.note: Both the project-level and global pretool-bash-safety.sh run on Bash commands (global via $HOME/.claude/hooks/, project via settings.json registration). This means Bash commands go through TWO safety checks, which is defense-in-depth.

section_6_hook_layering_summary.description: How hooks layer: global settings.json hooks + project settings.json hooks both apply

section_6_hook_layering_summary.execution_order: Global hooks fire first, then project hooks. A block at any layer stops the tool.
